_doc: Line budget for adws-pipeline/SKILL.md (SC-14/A3, F-83).
SKILL.md is the only always-resident file in the skill, so every line it carries is
paid on every load. NFR-3 caps it at 500 and frontmatter-lint has asserted that since
M-3b. What nothing asserted was the TREND. M-3b itself recorded '357 (SC-4), 367
(SC-5), 379 (SC-6) -- monotonic' and then bounded only the ceiling, which is the point
at which the file is already too large.
The evidence for this file: SC-10 cut SKILL.md from 425 to 337 and RECORDED that floor
as a decision (SC10_PLAN.md section 5: '337 with a 350-line advisory target is where
the prose stops being reference-grade'). SC-11, SC-12 and SC-13 then put back all 88
lines in about 24 hours. Nobody overrode the decision; nobody was asked to. Over 26
commits the file grew 25 times and shrank once.
This is a RATCHET, not a cap on growth. `budget` may be raised -- but only by editing
this file, with a reason, in the same commit that grows SKILL.md, where a reviewer
reads it. That is the whole mechanism: growth stays possible and stops being silent.
Three levels, all in frontmatter-lint.mjs:
NOTE  at 350   advisory target, unchanged from SC-10
FAIL  above `budget`
FAIL  at 500+  NFR-3, regardless of budget
WHAT THE LINT ACTUALLY ENFORCES, stated precisely because the first write-up of this
mechanism overclaimed it (review finding, 2026-08-09):
- SKILL.md may not exceed `budget`;
- `budget` must equal the LAST history entry, so raising the number without
recording anything fails;
- every entry carries `set_by`, `reason` and an integer `value`;
- history values are MONOTONIC, so the budget cannot be lowered to hide growth and
raised again later.
It does NOT enforce append-only. Rewriting the last history entry in place, rather
than appending a new one, passes the lint -- a file-local check cannot see the prior
state. What catches that is `git diff`: a rewrite shows as a MODIFIED line where an
append shows as an added one, which is exactly the signal a reviewer reads. The claim
is 'growth is recorded and visible in review', not 'the record cannot be forged'.
Lowering `budget` toward SC-10's 337 floor is a separate decision with a real prose
task attached; SC-14 deliberately did not take it. See DPPD.md section 23 (M-6).

history.reason: Seeded at the value observed by audit M-6, so the ratchet starts where the file actually was and requires no compression pass. SC-10's considered floor was 337; see _doc.

+5 for hard rule 9 (F-82): a reproduction.command is a record, never an execution channel. SC-13 shipped that rule as prose in artifact-layout.md alone, where the orchestrator that must honour it had no reason to look. Raising the budget in the same commit is this mechanism's first exercise, and the cost is now visible instead of absorbed.

+27 across three defects two live arm-A runs surfaced, all of which are rules the orchestrator must apply and therefore cannot live only in references/. +5 for the build gate assembling repo-context-scan's actual_changes from the worktree (F-84): the gate read the PLAN, so a builder writing outside allowed_paths passed on the plan's good intentions, and the live orchestrator caught it only because it checked the change set on its own initiative. +11 moving the drift gate ahead of the first git action and adding the receipt binding (F-85): grading the SHIPPED diff meant a BLOCK rewound a change that already had commits and a live PR, and no rewind can un-publish. +6 for running evidence-integrity.js at the terminal report (F-84b), which makes artifact-layout rule 9 executable after a live run wrote a placeholder timestamp that passed every gate. +5 on the validator map and the resumable prose the ordering change made wrong. This is the largest single raise since the ratchet was seeded and the first to buy safety ordering rather than a rule statement; the alternative was leaving three known-live defects documented but unenforced.

+12 for the halt lifecycle state (F-86), closing arm A gaps 4, 8 and 12 -- the only three of the twelve documented gaps that share one root cause. +9 for the section 5 preamble routing an operator halt INTO the terminal report, and +3 on the relay line. Both lines are orchestrator behaviour and cannot live only in references/: the orchestrator is the thing that must not abandon the tree mid-phase, and it is the thing that must tell the operator a RETRY verdict on their own deliberate stop means nothing failed. The mechanism this buys is gap 12's: carry_over is written at a terminal state, an operator halt produced no terminal state, so resumable:true was unreachable for a healthy run stopped on purpose -- the single best resume candidate the pipeline can produce. No policy said a halted run may not resume; there was simply no path to the record that would have said it could. The alternative to spending these lines was leaving three live runs' worth of evidence pointing at a hole nobody could reach from inside the document.
